snapshot.potentialHotelBusiness: Strong product and destination fit for intimate luxury leisure celebrations on Grand Anse Beach, rather than assumed corporate or city-centre demand. Kenwood explicitly sells this resort for weddings and vow renewals and says it books the whole wedding party, including guests. The resort publishes wedding capacity of up to 35 guests, beach/garden settings, on-resort planners and an all-inclusive honeymoon proposition. That 35-person figure is an event-capacity statement, not a room block or production forecast. Realistic pathway: UK couple enquiry → Kenwood wedding specialist qualifies dates, party and accommodation needs → resort confirms ceremony and suite availability → Kenwood confirms holiday bookings and introduces the in-resort coordinator → optional celebration enhancements are arranged. Additional guest accommodation and longer honeymoon stays are opportunities, not evidenced bookings.

establishedFacts: Kenwood has a dedicated Spice Island Beach Resort wedding page explicitly covering first weddings and renewal of vows.
Kenwood says it books the whole wedding party, including guests, and its general wedding process includes booking dates/hotel followed by introduction to the in-resort coordinator.
The resort’s own wedding page advertises up to 35 guests, beach/garden settings, full-service event staff and on-resort wedding planners.
The resort publishes Island Wedding, Spice Up Your Honeymoon and Vow Renewal packages plus optional wedding enhancements.
Janet Percy is identified in current profile evidence as Head of Weddings Product and Caribbean Product Manager and in Kenwood’s October 2026 company post as Head of Weddings.
Kenwood’s October 2026 company post identifies Manuela Fernández de Pinedo as Partnerships Marketing Executive participating in wedding promotion with destination and resort partners.
Kenwood’s terms require weddings to be booked with one of its holidays and generally describe confirmed wedding packages as non-refundable.
uncertainties: No specific dated wedding/group programme or committed room demand was verified; public marketing does not establish current production.
No named Kenwood Spice Island account manager, hotel-contracting signatory or dedicated group-operations owner was explicitly verified.
The current resort supply chain, trade rates, allocation, commission, credit terms and contractual counterparties are not established.
Historical account production, enquiry conversion, lead times, seasonality and room-night potential remain unknown.
Manuela’s exact internal title varies between company and personal profile sources; her partnership-marketing relevance is supported, not buying authority.
The named resort wedding coordinator, live package inclusions/prices, legal documentation and accessibility arrangements need reconfirmation.
qualificationQuestions: Who owns the Spice Island Beach Resort account and who may negotiate and sign its accommodation and wedding terms? Does Janet hold either responsibility?
Is accommodation contracted directly with the resort, through a wholesaler/bedbank, or on request? Who confirms ceremony inventory?
What wedding and vow-renewal enquiries, confirmed parties and attributable accommodation bookings has Kenwood actually produced, by travel period?
For the next real enquiry, what are the dates, flexibility, adults/children, rooms, categories and nights required? Is this couple-only or a travelling group?
What current ceremony/reception limits apply to each setup, and how does the published 35-guest capacity apply to resident and non-resident attendees?
What rates, minimum stays, group thresholds, deposits, release dates, cancellation terms, guest payment arrangements and commission/net-rate rules apply?
Which package elements are included in the all-inclusive stay, which are separately chargeable, who invoices them, and which revenues remain with the resort?
Who is the named in-resort wedding coordinator, and what are the confirmation, documentation and UK-to-resort handoff deadlines?
What current flight/transfer options, accessible-suite and ceremony access provisions, dietary support and weather backup can be confirmed for the actual party?
snapshot.recommendedNextStep: Develop the existing listed intermediary account rather than pitch a new unlisted property or invent a group programme. Ask the Kenwood wedding team to route a supplier/account discussion to Janet Percy. Request confirmation of the current Grenada/Spice Island product and contracting owners, existing sourcing arrangement, wedding enquiry conversion and attributable accommodation production. With the resort’s account owner/coordinator, validate current packages, capacity and guest-booking workflow; then agree a targeted UK wedding/vow-renewal sales brief and enquiry-to-booking handoff. Use Manuela for approved campaign activation only after commercial readiness is confirmed. Open a dated group opportunity only on receipt of a specific party brief; link its rooms and wedding components to the same account/opportunity to prevent double counting.

qualificationQuestions: Who owns the Spice Island Beach Resort account and who may negotiate and sign its accommodation and wedding terms? Does Janet hold either responsibility?
Is accommodation contracted directly with the resort, through a wholesaler/bedbank, or on request? Who confirms ceremony inventory?
What wedding and vow-renewal enquiries, confirmed parties and attributable accommodation bookings has Kenwood actually produced, by travel period?
For the next real enquiry, what are the dates, flexibility, adults/children, rooms, categories and nights required? Is this couple-only or a travelling group?
What current ceremony/reception limits apply to each setup, and how does the published 35-guest capacity apply to resident and non-resident attendees?
What rates, minimum stays, group thresholds, deposits, release dates, cancellation terms, guest payment arrangements and commission/net-rate rules apply?
Which package elements are included in the all-inclusive stay, which are separately chargeable, who invoices them, and which revenues remain with the resort?
Who is the named in-resort wedding coordinator, and what are the confirmation, documentation and UK-to-resort handoff deadlines?
What current flight/transfer options, accessible-suite and ceremony access provisions, dietary support and weather backup can be confirmed for the actual party?
commercialIntelligenceBrief.recommendedNextStep: Develop the existing listed intermediary account rather than pitch a new unlisted property or invent a group programme. Ask the Kenwood wedding team to route a supplier/account discussion to Janet Percy. Request confirmation of the current Grenada/Spice Island product and contracting owners, existing sourcing arrangement, wedding enquiry conversion and attributable accommodation production. With the resort’s account owner/coordinator, validate current packages, capacity and guest-booking workflow; then agree a targeted UK wedding/vow-renewal sales brief and enquiry-to-booking handoff. Use Manuela for approved campaign activation only after commercial readiness is confirmed. Open a dated group opportunity only on receipt of a specific party brief; link its rooms and wedding components to the same account/opportunity to prevent double counting.

approvedCustomerFacingDetail.hotelOpportunityThesis: Strong product and destination fit for intimate luxury leisure celebrations on Grand Anse Beach, rather than assumed corporate or city-centre demand. Kenwood explicitly sells this resort for weddings and vow renewals and says it books the whole wedding party, including guests. The resort publishes wedding capacity of up to 35 guests, beach/garden settings, on-resort planners and an all-inclusive honeymoon proposition. That 35-person figure is an event-capacity statement, not a room block or production forecast. Realistic pathway: UK couple enquiry → Kenwood wedding specialist qualifies dates, party and accommodation needs → resort confirms ceremony and suite availability → Kenwood confirms holiday bookings and introduces the in-resort coordinator → optional celebration enhancements are arranged. Additional guest accommodation and longer honeymoon stays are opportunities, not evidenced bookings.

qualificationQuestions: Who owns the Spice Island Beach Resort account and who may negotiate and sign its accommodation and wedding terms? Does Janet hold either responsibility?
Is accommodation contracted directly with the resort, through a wholesaler/bedbank, or on request? Who confirms ceremony inventory?
What wedding and vow-renewal enquiries, confirmed parties and attributable accommodation bookings has Kenwood actually produced, by travel period?
For the next real enquiry, what are the dates, flexibility, adults/children, rooms, categories and nights required? Is this couple-only or a travelling group?
What current ceremony/reception limits apply to each setup, and how does the published 35-guest capacity apply to resident and non-resident attendees?
What rates, minimum stays, group thresholds, deposits, release dates, cancellation terms, guest payment arrangements and commission/net-rate rules apply?
Which package elements are included in the all-inclusive stay, which are separately chargeable, who invoices them, and which revenues remain with the resort?
Who is the named in-resort wedding coordinator, and what are the confirmation, documentation and UK-to-resort handoff deadlines?
What current flight/transfer options, accessible-suite and ceremony access provisions, dietary support and weather backup can be confirmed for the actual party?

Use Manuela for approved campaign activation only after commercial readiness is confirmed. Open a dated group opportunity only on receipt of a specific party brief; link its rooms and wedding components to the same account/opportunity to prevent double counting.

The resort publishes wedding capacity of up to 35 guests, beach/garden settings, on-resort planners and an all-inclusive honeymoon proposition. That 35-person figure is an event-capacity statement, not a room block or production forecast. Realistic pathway: UK couple enquiry → Kenwood wedding specialist qualifies dates, party and accommodation needs → resort confirms ceremony and suite availability → Kenwood confirms holiday bookings and introduces the in-resort coordinator → optional celebration enhancements are arranged. Additional guest accommodation and longer honeymoon stays are opportunities, not evidenced bookings.

facts: Kenwood has a dedicated Spice Island Beach Resort wedding page explicitly covering first weddings and renewal of vows.
Kenwood says it books the whole wedding party, including guests, and its general wedding process includes booking dates/hotel followed by introduction to the in-resort coordinator.
The resort’s own wedding page advertises up to 35 guests, beach/garden settings, full-service event staff and on-resort wedding planners.
The resort publishes Island Wedding, Spice Up Your Honeymoon and Vow Renewal packages plus optional wedding enhancements.
Janet Percy is identified in current profile evidence as Head of Weddings Product and Caribbean Product Manager and in Kenwood’s October 2026 company post as Head of Weddings.
Kenwood’s October 2026 company post identifies Manuela Fernández de Pinedo as Partnerships Marketing Executive participating in wedding promotion with destination and resort partners.
Kenwood’s terms require weddings to be booked with one of its holidays and generally describe confirmed wedding packages as non-refundable.
uncertainties: No specific dated wedding/group programme or committed room demand was verified; public marketing does not establish current production.
No named Kenwood Spice Island account manager, hotel-contracting signatory or dedicated group-operations owner was explicitly verified.
The current resort supply chain, trade rates, allocation, commission, credit terms and contractual counterparties are not established.
Historical account production, enquiry conversion, lead times, seasonality and room-night potential remain unknown.
Manuela’s exact internal title varies between company and personal profile sources; her partnership-marketing relevance is supported, not buying authority.
The named resort wedding coordinator, live package inclusions/prices, legal documentation and accessibility arrangements need reconfirmation.

recommended_next_step.title: Recommended next step
recommended_next_step.body: Develop the existing listed intermediary account rather than pitch a new unlisted property or invent a group programme. Ask the Kenwood wedding team to route a supplier/account discussion to Janet Percy. Request confirmation of the current Grenada/Spice Island product and contracting owners, existing sourcing arrangement, wedding enquiry conversion and attributable accommodation production. With the resort’s account owner/coordinator, validate current packages, capacity and guest-booking workflow; then agree a targeted UK wedding/vow-renewal sales brief and enquiry-to-booking handoff. Use Manuela for approved campaign activation only after commercial readiness is confirmed. Open a dated group opportunity only on receipt of a specific party brief; link its rooms and wedding components to the same account/opportunity to prevent double counting.
qualificationQuestions: Who owns the Spice Island Beach Resort account and who may negotiate and sign its accommodation and wedding terms? Does Janet hold either responsibility?
Is accommodation contracted directly with the resort, through a wholesaler/bedbank, or on request? Who confirms ceremony inventory?
What wedding and vow-renewal enquiries, confirmed parties and attributable accommodation bookings has Kenwood actually produced, by travel period?
For the next real enquiry, what are the dates, flexibility, adults/children, rooms, categories and nights required? Is this couple-only or a travelling group?
What current ceremony/reception limits apply to each setup, and how does the published 35-guest capacity apply to resident and non-resident attendees?
What rates, minimum stays, group thresholds, deposits, release dates, cancellation terms, guest payment arrangements and commission/net-rate rules apply?
Which package elements are included in the all-inclusive stay, which are separately chargeable, who invoices them, and which revenues remain with the resort?
Who is the named in-resort wedding coordinator, and what are the confirmation, documentation and UK-to-resort handoff deadlines?
What current flight/transfer options, accessible-suite and ceremony access provisions, dietary support and weather backup can be confirmed for the actual party?
